subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity & model mix amendment for AtlasRetail
messages:
From: Dan Chen <dan.chen@atlasretail.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liz Morales <liz.morales@atlasretail.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — new model + reranker needs

Tessa,

We’re coming up on our 12-month renewal and have a few changes on our side that will materially change our capacity needs. High level: we want to add a larger long-context model (atlas-llama-70b-long, 64k token context) for checkout conversations, add a dedicated reranker pipeline for search (reranker queries ~= 2x per user interaction), and increase throughput guarantees for peak shopping hours.

Current baseline usage is roughly 180k daily active sessions; estimated peak concurrent sessions for the holiday spike is ~12k. For the new model we expect average prompt+response to be ~3k tokens (due to long context), and the reranker will add ~1.2 inference calls per session on average.

We need a proposal that covers:
- Reserved GPU pools for production & canary (capacity and burst)
- Throughput SLOs (p95/p99 targets, and failure fallbacks)
- Term options (12 vs 24 months) and delta to our current committed spend

I can share a sample workload CSV and our internal latency objectives — happy to join a call this week.

Attachments: Atlas_workload_snapshot_Mar2026.csv (summary)

Thanks,
Dan Chen
Director of ML Platform
AtlasRetail
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Dan Chen <dan.chen@atlasretail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — new model + reranker needs

Dan — appreciate the detail and the CSV. This is the right time to lock in capacity for holiday peaks. I’ve looped in Rishi (solutions) and Monica (CS) so we can scope the operational model and propose a formal amendment.

Quick asks before we size pools:
- Could you share a small sample of prompts (or the token distribution) for the atlas-llama-70b-long path? It helps us estimate KV cache and KV memory requirements.
- Is the reranker run synchronously in-path (impacting p99 for user-facing calls) or off-path (background ranking)?
- Target latency SLOs for both the long-context responses and reranker p99 (e.g., p99 < 500ms for user-facing, or p99 < 1.5s acceptable?)

Proposed next steps: quick tech sync with your infra team (30 min) + we’ll produce an amendment draft with capacity, throughput guarantees, and pricing options (12/24 month). Are you available Wed 10:00am PT?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Dan Chen <dan.chen@atlasretail.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liz Morales <liz.morales@atlasretail.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — new model + reranker needs

Tessa — Wed 10 works. Quick answers inline:
- I attached a brief sample (first_10k_prompts_sample.txt) and our token distribution in the CSV. Typical session has a 90th percentile of ~3.6k tokens for the long-context flow.
- The reranker is in-path for search suggestions (user waits on reranker) — it’s small models but high QPS. Expect reranker to add ~1.2 calls per session and a p99 target <= 400ms.
- For long-context path we’re shooting for p95 < 1s and p99 < 2s (we know 64k is heavy; looking for realistic targets and fallback plans).

Also attaching a short doc on our rollout plan and timeline (holiday promotional windows): we want the capacity live and validated by Oct 1, 2026.

Attachments: first_10k_prompts_sample.txt; Atlas_workload_snapshot_Mar2026.csv; Atlas_rollout_timeline.pdf

See you Wed.
Dan
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation — new model + reranker needs — internal sizing ask

Folks — forwarding Atlas’ notes + samples. Key asks: 64k context model + in-path reranker; p99 targets we quoted above; Oct 1 validation deadline.

Can we:
1) Draft an amendment (v1) that enumerates reserved pool sizes (prod + canary + burst), throughput guarantees, and term pricing (12 vs 24). Put numbers in atlas_draft_amendment_v1.xlsx.
2) Rishi — can you provide a mapping from Atlas’ workload -> recommended GPU counts (A100-80GB equiv), KV cache sizing, and any operational constraints (e.g., cold-start behavior, canary policy)?
3) Dev — if we offer a fallback model variant (smaller context or quantized), what are the expected latencies and quality delta we should show in the proposal?

No need for legal to see this yet — want a tight engineering-backed estimate before the commercial write-up.

Thanks — Tessa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal conversation — sizing and operational recommendations

Team — ran a quick pass on the sample and CSV. High level recommendations (short):
- Production reserved pool: 48 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (this accounts for 64k KV working sets, sustained decoding, and headroom for holiday peaks).
- Canary / validation pool: 6 GPUs (same class) for staged rollouts and perf validation.
- Burst / transient pool configurable up to additional 12 GPUs for short spikes (5–10 min windows).

Throughput & SLOs:
- Recommend contract throughput guarantee: 95th percentile for holiday windows expressed as a requests/minute commitment (we can commit to 7,500 reqs/min sustained during 4-hour peak windows; burst capacity available).
- Latency objective: for in-path reranker p99 <= 450 ms achievable with a dedicated small-GPU pool + batching; for atlas-llama-70b-long p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~1.9–2.2s depending on sequence lengths and tokenization.

Cost/term guidance:
- Estimated incremental committed spend: +~34% vs their current reserved spend for a 12-month term. A 24-month commit reduces incremental by ~14% (volume discount + capacity planning benefit).
- We should include a higher-rate overage pricing and an automated fallback policy: if p99 latency > SLA for >3 consecutive 10-min windows, traffic automatically shifts to a smaller quantized model with prefabricated prompt templates (quality delta ~ 4–6% on synthetic eval).

Operational notes:
- KV memory: plan for 1.2TB of distributed KV cache across the pool (rough order).
- Canary plan: 10% traffic for 48 hours, verify perf/quality; then step to 50% for 24 hours before full cutover.

I’ll populate atlas_draft_amendment_v1.xlsx with GPU counts, a simple cost table (12/24 mo), and a suggested SLA clause.

—Rishi
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Dan Chen <dan.chen@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Liz Morales <liz.morales@atlasretail.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: AtlasRetail renewal amendment (summary & next steps)

Dan — thanks again for the sync. Attached is a short summary and a draft amendment (redline). Highlights: 

- Capacity: reserved pool of 48 A100-80GB equiv GPU units for production; 6 GPU canary pool; 12 GPU burst capacity configurable.
- SLA & throughput: contracted sustained holiday peak commitment of 7,500 reqs/min for 4-hour windows with burst headroom. Latency objectives documented (reranker p99 <= 450ms; long-context p95/p99 numbers listed).
- Fallbacks: automated traffic shift to a smaller, quantized variant if SLA violation thresholds are met. We include a quality/regression monitoring plan with sample prompt evals.
- Term & pricing: 12-month amendment = +34% incremental to current committed spend. 24-month term reduces incremental to +20% with additional capacity planning credits. Full cost table in atlas_draft_amendment_v1.xlsx.

Attachments: atlas_draft_amendment_v1.xlsx; Atlas_renewal_redline_v1.pdf

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached redline and cost table — flag any commercial/tech concerns in-line by Tue EOD.
2) If green, we’ll route the amendment to your procurement and legal for redlines (we can turn around a DocuSign-ready version in 3 business days).
3) Kick off an ops validation calendar item for the Canary testing (Rishi will own).

DocuSign (provisional link): https://docusign.redwood.ai/ATLAS-RENEW-2026 (will be enabled after commercial sign-off)

If you’d like to take this live in a short call, happy to schedule one this week.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
